record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: Consider an entire product in C^n with planar zeros, pi(z) = product_{k>=1} g(<z,a_k>|a_k|^{-2},p), where g(u,p) = (1-u) exp(u + u^2/2 + ... + u^p/p) for p != 0 and g(u,0) = 1-u, and where the sequence a_k has genus p through sum |a_k|^{-p-1} < infinity and sum |a_k|^{-p} = infinity. Existing sufficient conditions for bounded L-index in a direction assume the zero-defining vectors lie on a fixed ray, a_kj = m_j |a_k|. Are there sufficient conditions for bounded L-index in a direction for such products without imposing that fixed-ray condition?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $p\geq 0$, define the Weierstrass primary factor
$$g(u,p)=\begin{cases}1-u,& p=0,\\ (1-u)\exp\!\left(u+\tfrac{u^2}{2}+\cdots+\tfrac{u^p}{p}\right),& p\geq 1.\end{cases}$$
Let $n\geq 2$ and let $(a_k)_{k\geq 1}\subset \mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ be a sequence with genus $p$, i.e.
$$\sum_{k\geq 1}|a_k|^{-(p+1)}<\infty,\qquad \sum_{k\geq 1}|a_k|^{-p}=\infty,$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{C}^n$. Consider the canonical product with "planar" zero set
$$\pi(z)=\prod_{k\geq 1} g\!\left(\tfrac{\langle z,a_k\rangle}{|a_k|^{2}},\,p\right),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}^n,$$
where $\langle z,a\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^n z_j\overline{a_j}$. Fix a direction $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and a positive continuous function $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$. An entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and all $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$,
$$\frac{|\partial^{\,m}_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\;\leq\;\max_{0\leq k\leq N}\frac{|\partial^{\,k}_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k},$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\,\partial F/\partial z_j$. The least such $N$ is the $L$-index of $F$ in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.

Known sufficient conditions guaranteeing that $\pi$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ have been established under the additional hypothesis that all vectors $a_k$ lie on a single fixed ray, i.e. $a_{k,j}=m_j|a_k|$ for some fixed unit vector $(m_1,\dots,m_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $k$.

Problem: Without imposing this fixed-ray restriction on the sequence $(a_k)$, find sufficient conditions on $(a_k)$, $\mathbf{b}$, and $L$ under which the canonical product $\pi$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Bandura, Skaskiv and collaborators has produced sufficient conditions for boundedness of L-index in a direction for entire functions with "plane" zeros, but the available sources do not clearly confirm whether the fixed-ray hypothesis on the zero-defining vectors $a_k$ has been removed in the canonical-product setting described. The status of this specific problem could not be definitively verified from the search results.

status_evidence.title: Slice Holomorphic Functions in Several Variables with Bounded L-Index in Direction
status_evidence.snippet: Criteria for slice holomorphic functions of bounded L-index in direction describing distribution of zeros and logarithmic derivative behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues on sufficient/necessary conditions for bounded L-index in a direction, including zero-distribution criteria.

status_evidence.title: Entire functions of several variables of bounded index
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on entire functions of several variables of bounded L-index in joint variables and in a direction.
status_evidence.claim: The framework treats entire products with planar zeros; explicit fixed-ray-free criteria are not stated.

status_evidence.title: Some criteria of boundedness of the L-index in direction for slice holomorphic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes criteria of bounded L-index in direction for slice holomorphic functions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent criteria address related but not identical settings, leaving the planar-zero canonical-product problem without an explicit resolution.
